title: Structured Driving-State Narratives for Small Language Model-Based GNSS Spoofing Detection
abstract: arXiv:2608.17092v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) depend on reliable Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning. However, spoofed GNSS signals can induce plausible but incorrect vehicle states. This study develops a small language model (SLM)-based framework for detecting and classifying GNSS spoofing attacks by comparing vehicle behaviors independently derived from GNSS and other sensing sources. The framework converts independent driving states from GNSS and other sensing sources into structured semantic narratives that are provided to an SLM for spoofing detection and attack classification. The performance of the SLM-based framework is compared with large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned on identical training data and evaluated on the same test set. The evaluation considers five classes: no attack, overshoot attack, stopped attack, turn-by-turn attack, and wrong-turn attack. The framework is also evaluated with geographically unseen field data

translated_title: 基于小语言模型的GNSS欺骗检测的结构化驾驶状态叙事
translated_abstract: 自主驾驶车辆（AVs）依赖可靠的全球导航卫星系统（GNSS）定位。然而，欺骗的GNSS信号可能诱导出看似合理但错误的车辆状态。本研究开发了一个基于小语言模型（SLM）的框架，通过比较从GNSS和其他传感源独立得出的车辆行为来检测和分类GNSS欺骗攻击。该框架将从GNSS和其他传感源获得的独立驾驶状态转换为结构化语义叙事，提供给SLM进行欺骗检测和攻击分类。SLM框架的性能与在相同训练数据上微调并在相同测试集上评估的大型语言模型（LLMs）进行了比较。评估考虑了五类情况：无攻击、超调攻击、停止攻击、逐向攻击和错误转向攻击。该框架还使用地理上未见过的实地数据进行了评估。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于小语言模型的GNSS欺骗检测框架，通过将独立驾驶状态转换为结构化叙事，实现了高效且准确的多类欺骗攻击检测与分类。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an SLM-based GNSS spoofing detection framework that converts independent driving states into structured narratives, achieving efficient and accurate detection and classification of multiple spoofing attack types.
